title: Sparse top-k Mirror LoRA atoms
hypothesis: Input-conditioned gating over logical LoRA experts can be aggregated into coefficients over a shared rank-1 atom bank; selecting the top-k atoms per input can preserve output quality while reducing active adapter compute and full expert-bank bytes. Mirror-specific value requires beating native sparse low-rank factor execution.
physical_object: Shared bank of sixteen rank-1 LoRA atoms plus sixteen logical expert coefficient vectors
mirror_coordinate: Input-conditioned sparse top-k selection over gate-aggregated atom coordinates
logical_multiplicity: Sixteen logical LoRA experts and per-input sparse atom mixtures

task.metric: held-out output NRMSE, actual serialized payload bytes, active MAC proxy, CPU wall time

controls: Full dense MoLE expert bank with all experts active
Full dense MoLE with top-2 expert routing
Shared atom bank with top-k aggregated coefficients
Native sparse low-rank atom execution with identical selection rule and factors

storage.authority: Actual serialized complete inference payload bytes

success_gate: At some k<16, output NRMSE <=0.02 and complete bytes <=60% of full expert bank; active MACs must improve over full MoLE. Mirror-specific success requires strict Pareto gain over native sparse low-rank control.
failure_gate: Quality/storage gate miss or exact native sparse factor alias without strict Pareto gain; fresh remains sealed after exact alias.
boundaries: Router is fixed random input-conditioned softmax; this isolates representation/execution rather than learned routing
No task capacity claim from logical expert count
All charged arrays included in actual NPZ payload
Top-k atom indices are computed at inference and not stored
